concise_function: FLC EXPRESSOR; component of the FRIGIDA (FRI) activator complex that up-regulates the floral repressor FLC.
Flowering_time_interpretation: Core flowering-time regulator. FLX is required for FRI-dependent activation of FLC; loss of FLX reduces FLC expression and causes early flowering, whereas increased FLX activity would be expected to enhance FLC, delay flowering, and strengthen vernalization requirement.

concise_function: Adapter subunit of SCF E3 ubiquitin ligases; partners with multiple F-box proteins including those in phyA light signaling (EID1/AFR) and circadian clock–related complexes (ADO1/2/3).
Flowering_time_interpretation: Integrates light and circadian cues that feed into the CONSTANS–FT flowering pathway. Allelic changes affecting specific SCF complexes (e.g. phyA or clock-linked F-box proteins) could alter photoperiod sensitivity or phase of flowering, likely with pleiotropic effects on hormone responses and development.

concise_function: BTB/E3-ligase adaptor that binds and targets ACS5 (ACC synthase) for degradation, thereby restraining ethylene biosynthesis.
Flowering_time_interpretation: Regulator of ethylene levels, which in turn modulate gibberellin and floral transition. eto1 loss-of-function or reduced activity causes ethylene overproduction; ethylene can lower GA and delay flowering, especially under certain environmental conditions. Natural or selected variation at ETO1 could shift flowering time via hormone balance.

concise_function: Ca²⁺-regulated protein kinase that acts with CBL sensors; part of the CBL–CIPK network integrating Ca²⁺, abiotic stress, and hormone (ABA/auxin/ethylene/JA) signaling.
Flowering_time_interpretation: Plausible **modifier** of flowering time via stress and hormone signaling rather than a canonical floral integrator. CBL–CIPK modules regulate responses to drought, salinity and ABA, and these pathways are known to shift flowering time under stress; variation in CIPK5 could influence stress-induced acceleration or delay of flowering, particularly in stressful or marginal environments.
